the metabolism of the antibacterial agent TCC.
the metabolic activation of the antimicrobial agent TCC by the CYP1A enzymes yielding glutathione adducts.

the antibacterial agent triclocarban is metabolized by cytochrome P-450 1A to a reactive metabolite which covalently binds to protein in human keratinocytes.

CYP1A is the main cytochrome P-450 enzyme that metabolizes triclosan and triclocarban.
the antibacterial compound, TCC, is metabolized to a reactive species that binds covalently to protein and that this reaction occurs in human keratinocytes, which are the main cell type in the skin.
